If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment remains flat (0.33–0.67) over last 5 days, apply no correction for early horizon, but reduce forecast by 0.5–1% in late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen overfitting.

If sentiment is positive but recent price action shows divergence (forecast > true for 3+ days), reduce forecast by 0.5–1% in mid-horizon to correct for overconfidence.

If sentiment is negative but recent price action shows divergence (forecast < true for 3+ days), increase forecast by 0.5–1% in mid-horizon to correct for underestimation.
